 519: 
 520: \begin{theorem}[Arbitrary-order law-by-law tail-defect decomposition]
 521: \label{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}
 522: Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), and let \(r\ge1\) be an integer.  Let
 523: \(\nu,\eta\) be probability laws on \(\RR^d\) satisfying
 524: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-moment-hypotheses}
 525:  m_\gamma(\nu)=m_\gamma(\eta)\quad(|\gamma|<r),
 526:  \qquad
 527:  \int_{\RR^d}|x|^r(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
 528: \end{equation}
 529: For \(\lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\}\), put
 530: \[
 531:  \tau_s^\lambda=\lambda(|x|>s),\qquad
 532:  V_s^\lambda(y)=\int_{\{|x|>s\}}
 533:  F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),
 534: \]
 535: and use the moment modes \(B_j^\lambda\) from
 536: \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-moment-modes}.  Their values agree for \(j<r\);
 537: write
 538: \[
 539:  C_{r-1,s}(y)=\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_j^\nu(y)
 540:              =\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_j^\eta(y),
 541: \]
 542: with an empty sum when \(r=1\), and define
 543: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-quotients}
 544:  A_s^\lambda(y)=1+C_{r-1,s}(y)+V_s^\lambda(y)-\tau_s^\lambda.
 545: \end{equation}
 546: For all sufficiently large \(s\), both \(A_s^\lambda\) are positive,
 547: integrate to one against \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), and hence define probability
 548: densities
 549: \[
 550:  k_{r,s}^\lambda(x)=s^{-d}p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)
 551:                     A_s^\lambda(x/s).
 552: \]
 553:  The explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy
 554: \begin{align}
 555:  \mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)
 556:  &:=D_{\rm KL}(k_{r,s}^\nu\|k_{r,s}^\eta)\notag\\
 557:  &=\int_{\RR^d}A_s^\eta
 558:  \Phi\!\left(\frac{A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta}{A_s^\eta}\right)
 559:  \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
 560:  \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-energy}
 561: \end{align}
 562: is finite, and, with
 563: \(\Delta_r=\int x^{\otimes r}(\nu-\eta)(\dd x)\), one has
 564: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition}
 565:  D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 566:  =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
 567:   +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
 568: \end{equation}
 569: In particular, law by law,
 570: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-criterion}
 571:  s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 572:  \longrightarrow\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
 573:  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 574:  s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
 575: \end{equation}
 576: No regular-variation or absolute-continuity hypothesis, and no moment above
 577: order \(r\), is required.
 578: \end{theorem}
 579: 
 580: \begin{proof}
 581: Write \(p_1=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\), \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), and let
 582: \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be the homogeneous degree-\(j\) Taylor term of
 583: \(F_y(z)\) at zero.  The stable-kernel estimates in
 584: Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package}, Taylor's formula, and
 585: translation continuity of \(D^rp_1\) in \(L^1\) give, for \(|z|\le1\),
 586: \begin{align}
 587:  &\left\|F_\cdot(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r\mathsf B_j(\cdot,z)\right\|_\infty
 588:  +\left\|F_\cdot(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r\mathsf B_j(\cdot,z)
 589:   \right\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
 590:  \le\varepsilon_r(|z|)|z|^r,
 591:  \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder}\\
 592:  &\|\mathsf B_j(\cdot,z)\|_\infty
 593:  +\|\mathsf B_j(\cdot,z)\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
 594:  \le C_r|z|^j,\qquad 1\le j\le r,
 595:  \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds}
 596: \end{align}
 597: where \(\varepsilon_r\) is bounded on \([0,1]\) and tends to zero at
 598: zero.  For the uniform part one may use the bounded order-\((r+1)\)
 599: derivative quotient, giving the stronger \(O(|z|^{r+1})\) bound.  For the
 600: \(L^1\) part, multiplication by \(p_1(y)\) reduces the integral remainder
 601: to translates of \(D^rp_1\), exactly as in
 602: \eqref{eq:stable-local-taylor-modulus}.
 603: 
 604: Set
 605: \[
 606:  q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
 607: \]
 608: Splitting the integral at \(|x|=s\), retaining the raw exterior translate,
 609: and using the moment identities gives the exact decomposition
 610: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-exact-quotient-split}
 611:  q_s^\lambda=A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}B_r^\lambda+R_s^\lambda.
 612: \end{equation}
 613: Here \(R_s^\lambda\) is the interior Taylor remainder through order \(r\)
 614: minus the exterior Taylor modes of orders \(1,\ldots,r\).  Equations
 615: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} and
 616: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} imply
 617: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-remainder-smallness}
 618:  \|R_s^\lambda\|_\infty+
 619:  \|R_s^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
 620: \end{equation}
 621: Indeed, after multiplication by \(s^r\), the interior term is dominated by
 622: \(C|x|^r\) and converges pointwise to zero, while for \(j\le r\),
 623: \[
 624:  s^{-j}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^j\lambda(\dd x)
 625:  \le s^{-r}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x)=o(s^{-r}).
 626: \]
 627: The same last estimate gives
 628: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-mass-smallness}
 629:  \tau_s^\lambda=o(s^{-r}).
 630: \end{equation}
 631: 
 632: Translation preserves mass, so
 633: \[
 634:  V_s^\lambda\ge0,\qquad
 635:  \int V_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=\tau_s^\lambda.
 636: \]
 637: Also \(\int B_j^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0\), by integration of the
 638: derivatives in \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-moment-modes}.  Therefore
 639: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-normalization}
 640:  \int A_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=1.
 641: \end{equation}
 642: Moreover,
 643: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-lower-bound}
 644:  \inf_yA_s^\lambda(y)
 645:  \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-\tau_s^\lambda\longrightarrow1,
 646: \end{equation}
 647: because \(V_s^\lambda\ge0\),
 648: \(\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty=O(s^{-1})\) (with value zero when \(r=1\)), and
 649: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mass-smallness} holds.  This proves positivity,
 650: including at \(r=1\), and gives a common lower bound such as \(1/2\).
 651: 
 652: We next prove proxy-entropy finiteness without appealing to the covariance
 653: case.  The two-sided stable-density bound in
 654: Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package} and
 655: \(1+|w+z|\le(1+|w|)(1+|z|)\) give
 656: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-stable-translate-entropy}
 657:  D_{\rm KL}\!\left(p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)\,\middle\|\,p_1\right)
 658:  \le C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|z|).
 659: \end{equation}
 660: If \(\tau_s^\lambda>0\), write \(V_s^\lambda=\tau_s^\lambda Q_s^\lambda\),
 661: where \(Q_s^\lambda\) is the quotient, relative to \(p_1\), of the
 662: normalized exterior translate mixture.  Convexity of relative entropy and
 663: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-stable-translate-entropy} imply
 664: \begin{align}
 665:  \int Q_s^\lambda\log Q_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
 666:  &\le\frac1{\tau_s^\lambda}\int_{|x|>s}
 667:  \left\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|x|/s)\right\}
 668:  \lambda(\dd x)\notag\\
 669:  &<\infty,
 670:  \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}
 671: \end{align}
 672: since \(\log(1+|x|/s)\le |x|/s\) and the assumed \(r\)-th moment, with
 673: \(r\ge1\), supplies a finite first moment.  For \(0\le\tau\le1\),
 674: \(\Phi(\tau q)\le\tau q\log(1+q)\); hence
 675: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}, together with the bound
 676: of the negative part of \(q\log q\), proves
 677: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-potential-entropy-finite}
 678:  \int\Phi(V_s^\lambda)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}<\infty.
 679: \end{equation}
 680: The conclusion is immediate when \(\tau_s^\lambda=0\).
 681: 
 682: For large \(s\), \(|C_{r-1,s}-\tau_s^\lambda|\le1/2\), so
 683: \(A_s^\lambda\le3/2+V_s^\lambda\).  The elementary bound
 684: \[
 685:  (u+v)\log^+(u+v)\le C\{1+v+\Phi(v)\},
 686:  \qquad 0\le u\le3/2,\quad v\ge0,
 687: \]
 688: and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-potential-entropy-finite} show that
 689: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-entropy-finite}
 690:  \int A_s^\lambda\log^+A_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}<\infty.

The theorem is a specialization of the unnumbered abstract kernel theorem
that precedes it.  For a strictly positive density \(p\), the proof uses only
bounded normalized derivatives through order \(r\), uniform
translation-continuity of the normalized order-\(r\) derivative, and an
order-\(r\) bound on the entropy of a translate of \(p\).  These conditions
hold for all isotropic strictly stable densities, for the Poisson kernel, and
for every multivariate Student density \(c_{\beta,d}(1+|y|^2)^{-\beta/2}\),
\(\beta>d\).  No tail asymptotic or regular variation enters the abstract
proof.  The Gaussian density does not satisfy the bounded normalized-jet
condition: its normalized derivatives are Hermite polynomials, and an
additive common jet need not remain positive.  Thus the Gaussian
first-unmatched-moment theorem recalled above uses a different weighted
Hermite mechanism; it is not presented as a member of the positive
tail-proxy theorem.

   1: \begin{corollary}[A sufficient moment condition for defect vanishing]
   2: \label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
   3: Under the hypotheses of
   4: Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, suppose in
   5: addition that \(\Delta_r\ne0\) and
   6: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition}
   7:  \int_{\RR^d}|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
   8: \end{equation}
   9: Then
  10: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}
  11:  s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
  12: \end{equation}
  13: This condition includes noncompact pairs of laws.
  14: \end{corollary}
  15: 
  16: \begin{proof}
  17: Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} and
  18: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} give, respectively,
  19: \begin{align*}
  20:  D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
  21:  &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),\\
  22:  D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
  23:  &=\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
  24:    +\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
  25: \end{align*}
  26: Subtracting proves \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-limit}.
  27: 
  28: For a concrete noncompact class, use the finite-support probability blocks
  29: from Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks}.  Convolve \(A_R^+\) and
  30: \(A_R^-\) with the same nondegenerate Gaussian law.  The multinomial formula
  31: shows that the convolved laws still match below order \(r\), while their
  32: order-\(r\) difference is the nonzero difference of the two blocks: every
  33: other term contains a block-moment difference of order below \(r\).  Both
  34: convolved laws are noncompact and have moments of every order, so
  35: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-positive-moment-condition} applies.
  36: \end{proof}
  37: 
  38: \begin{corollary}[Non-vacuousness of the tail-defect criterion]
  39: \label{cor:arbitrary-tail-defect-nonvacuousness}
  40: If \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
  41: \(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\) with
  42: finite \(\rho\)-th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment below
  43: order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference, for
  44: which
  45: \begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}
  46:  \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)=+\infty.
  47: \end{equation}
  48: In particular, vanishing of the explicit nonnegative tail-defect energy is
  49: not automatic under the minimal finite \(r\)-th moment hypothesis.
  50: \end{corollary}
  51: 
  52: \begin{proof}
  53: Use the laws in the sharpness assertion
  54: \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  They satisfy the hypotheses of the
  55: law-by-law decomposition because \(\rho\ge r\).  Multiplying
  56: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition} by \(s^{2r}\) gives
  57: \[
  58:  s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
  59:  =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
  60:   +s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(1).
  61: \]
  62: The quadratic term is finite and independent of \(s\), whereas the left
  63: side has infinite limsup by \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  This
  64: forces \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-unbounded-limsup}.
  65: \end{proof}

from pathlib import Path
import re
import unittest


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
INPUT_RE = re.compile(r"\\input\{([^}]+)\}")


def read_tex_source(path: Path) -> str:
    """Read a TeX source together with any local input wrappers."""

    source = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    def expand(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
        child = ROOT / match.group(1)
        if child.suffix == "":
            child = child.with_suffix(".tex")
        return read_tex_source(child)

    return INPUT_RE.sub(expand, source)


class StableSpineManuscriptTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_main_article_keeps_the_restored_article_architecture(self) -> None:
        main = (ROOT / "main.tex").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

        self.assertIn(r"\input{sec_verified_A2_results}", main)
        self.assertIn(r"\input{bibliography_shared}", main)
        self.assertNotIn(r"\input{sec_stable_entropy_spine}", main)
        for article_input in (
            r"\input{sec_entropy_asymptotics}",
            r"\input{sec_entropy_30_eighth_defect_layer}",
            r"\input{sec_gram_space}",
            r"\input{sec_strip_00_poisson_image}",
            r"\input{sec_strip_20_symbol_sampling}",
            r"\input{sec_strip_30_cardinal_observation}",
        ):
            self.assertIn(article_input, main)

    def test_stable_tail_decomposition_is_stated_and_proved(self) -> None:
        theorem_path = ROOT / "sec_verified_A2_results.tex"
        theorem_source = read_tex_source(theorem_path)

        required = (
            r"\label{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition}",

            r"\|R_s\|_\infty+\|R_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-2})",
            r"\int V_s^\nu\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=\tau_s",
            r"No regular-variation, absolute-continuity, or moment hypothesis above order two",
        )
        for text in required:
            self.assertIn(text, theorem_source)

    def test_decomposition_theorem_has_one_source(self) -> None:
        label = r"\label{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition}"
        sources = list(ROOT.glob("*.tex"))
        occurrences = sum(
            path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").count(label) for path in sources
        )
        self.assertEqual(occurrences, 1)

\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below
order \(r\), and satisfy \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  For all large \(s\),
the corresponding additively normalized proxy with \(H=0\) satisfies
\[
 \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
 \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
 \qquad
 A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
\]
Consequently,
\[
 A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
 =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
 \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
 \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
\]
The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
\[
 D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
 =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
   +o(s^{-2r}),
\]
whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
actual smoothed entropy coefficient
\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
class boundary is not a proof artifact.

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
+bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

since \(\log(1+|x|/s)\le |x|/s\) and the assumed \(r\)-th moment, with

\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-potential-entropy-finite}

\end{equation}
The conclusion is immediate when \(\tau_s^\lambda=0\).

For large \(s\), \(|C_{r-1,s}-\tau_s^\lambda|\le1/2\), so
\(A_s^\lambda\le3/2+V_s^\lambda\).  The elementary bound
\[
 (u+v)\log^+(u+v)\le C\{1+v+\Phi(v)\},
 \qquad 0\le u\le3/2,\quad v\ge0,
\]
and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-potential-entropy-finite} show that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-entropy-finite}
 \int A_s^\lambda\log^+A_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}<\infty.
\end{equation}
Finally \(A_s^\eta\ge1/2\).  The positive part of
\(A_s^\nu\log(A_s^\nu/A_s^\eta)\) is bounded by
\(A_s^\nu\log^+(2A_s^\nu)\), while its negative part is bounded in absolute
integral by \(e^{-1}\int A_s^\eta\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=e^{-1}\).
Thus \(\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)<\infty\), as asserted.

It remains to verify, rather than assume, the hypotheses of the abstract
two-background KL perturbation lemma.  Put
\(\epsilon_s=s^{-r}\), take
\[
 (A_{1,s},A_{2,s})=(A_s^\nu,A_s^\eta),\qquad
 (B_{1,s},B_{2,s})=(B_r^\nu,B_r^\eta),
 \qquad (R_{1,s},R_{2,s})=(R_s^\nu,R_s^\eta).
\]
The modes \(B_r^\lambda\) are bounded by
\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds}, and their integrals vanish.  The first
requested background estimate follows directly from the common jet and the
exact tail normalization:
\begin{align}
 \|A_s^\lambda-1\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
 &\le\|C_{r-1,s}\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
      +\|V_s^\lambda-\tau_s^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\notag\\
 &\le \sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}\|B_j^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
      +2\tau_s^\lambda=o(1).
 \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-background-to-one}
\end{align}
For \(r=1\), the sum is empty and the same proof applies.  For the second
background estimate, the common jet cancels exactly, and therefore
\begin{align}
 \|A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
 &\le\|V_s^\nu-V_s^\eta\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
       +|\tau_s^\nu-\tau_s^\eta|\notag\\
 &\le2(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
 \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-two-background-separation}
\end{align}
This is the place where retaining the common lower-order jet removes every
interior contribution from the difference of the backgrounds.

The proxy lower bound is \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-lower-bound}.
For the actual quotient, the bounded logarithmic gradient of \(p_1\) gives
\(F_y(z)\ge e^{-L|z|}\), uniformly in \(y\).  Jensen's inequality then yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-quotient-positive-lower-bound}
 q_s^\lambda(y)
 \ge\int e^{-L|x|/s}\lambda(\dd x)
 \ge e^{-L\EE_\lambda|X|/s}\longrightarrow1
\end{equation}
uniformly in \(y\).  Thus the actual quotients have a common positive lower
bound.  Their exact split is
\(q_s^\lambda=A_s^\lambda+\epsilon_sB_r^\lambda+R_s^\lambda\),
and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-remainder-smallness} supplies the required
\(L^1\) and \(L^\infty\) smallness.  Finally,
\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-entropy-finite} verifies the finite
positive entropy hypothesis.  All hypotheses of the two-background KL
perturbation lemma are now proved.  Its conclusion gives
\[
 D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 =\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)
 +\frac{s^{-2r}}2\int(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta)^2
       \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}+o(s^{-2r}).
\]
By \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-leading-mode},
\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the quadratic integral is
\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves
\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition}.  Formula
\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-energy} is a relative \(\Phi\)-entropy and
is therefore nonnegative; the equivalence
\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-criterion} follows immediately.

The raw-tail split, its normalization, and the finite-moment dominated
convergence are exactly the steps that survive from the covariance proof.
The new step is the two-background expansion above: it retains the common
lower-order jet inside both positive tail proxies and replaces the
unavailable one-sided \(\Phi\)-energy of a signed tail difference by a
relative \(\Phi\)-energy.  When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is
centred, this energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\),
which differs from the energy in
Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by \(o(s^{-4})\), as shown
 in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
\end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the

+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
+bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
+\item invertible affine images;
+\item finite tensor products, allowing different block dimensions; and
+\item finite positive mixtures of admissible densities on the same space.
+\end{enumerate}

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
+bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
+bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

+\begin{proof}
+Choose \(j\) with \(\gamma_j>0\), put
+\(f=\partial^{\gamma-e_j}p\in W^{1,1}\), and test

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Bounded score implies finite translate entropy]
+\label{lem:bounded-score-translate-entropy}
+If \(p>0\), \(p\in C^1(\RR^d)\), and
+\(\|\nabla\log p\|_\infty\le L\), then, for every \(z\in\RR^d\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:bounded-score-translate-entropy}
+ 0\le D_{\rm KL}\bigl(p(\mathord\cdot-z)\|p\bigr)\le L|z|.
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+After the change of variables \(w=y-z\), the divergence is
+\(\int p(w)\log\{p(w)/p(w+z)\}\dd w\).  The fundamental theorem of
+calculus bounds the absolute value of the logarithm by \(L|z|\); integration
+and nonnegativity of relative entropy give
+\eqref{eq:bounded-score-translate-entropy}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}

+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
+bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the

+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
+\item invertible affine images;
+\item finite tensor products, allowing different block dimensions; and
+\item finite positive mixtures of admissible densities on the same space.
+\end{enumerate}

+therefore applies to every kernel obtained by finitely combining these

+strictly \(\alpha\)-stable density, \(0<\alpha<2\), the Poisson kernel in
+every dimension, and every multivariate Student kernel
 \[

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the

+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.

-Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by \(o(s^{-4})\), as shown
- in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
+When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is centred, the identified
+energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), which differs
+from the energy in Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by
+\(o(s^{-4})\), as shown in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
 \end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
+\item invertible affine images;
+\item finite tensor products, allowing different block dimensions; and
+\item finite positive mixtures of admissible densities on the same space.
+\end{enumerate}
+The criterion of Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel}
+therefore applies to every kernel obtained by finitely combining these
+operations.  Its base members include, at every order, each isotropic
+strictly \(\alpha\)-stable density, \(0<\alpha<2\), the Poisson kernel in
+every dimension, and every multivariate Student kernel
 \[

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
+bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

- \int A_s^\lambda\log^+A_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}<\infty.
-\end{equation}
-Finally \(A_s^\eta\ge1/2\).  The positive part of
-\(A_s^\nu\log(A_s^\nu/A_s^\eta)\) is bounded by
-\(A_s^\nu\log^+(2A_s^\nu)\), while its negative part is bounded in absolute
-integral by \(e^{-1}\int A_s^\eta\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=e^{-1}\).
-Thus \(\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)<\infty\), as asserted.
-
-It remains to verify, rather than assume, the hypotheses of the abstract
-two-background KL perturbation lemma.  Put
-\(\epsilon_s=s^{-r}\), take
-\[
- (A_{1,s},A_{2,s})=(A_s^\nu,A_s^\eta),\qquad
- (B_{1,s},B_{2,s})=(B_r^\nu,B_r^\eta),
- \qquad (R_{1,s},R_{2,s})=(R_s^\nu,R_s^\eta).
-\]
-The modes \(B_r^\lambda\) are bounded by
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds}, and their integrals vanish.  The first
-requested background estimate follows directly from the common jet and the
-exact tail normalization:
-\begin{align}
- \|A_s^\lambda-1\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
- &\le\|C_{r-1,s}\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
-      +\|V_s^\lambda-\tau_s^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\notag\\
- &\le \sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}\|B_j^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
-      +2\tau_s^\lambda=o(1).
- \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-background-to-one}
-\end{align}
-For \(r=1\), the sum is empty and the same proof applies.  For the second
-background estimate, the common jet cancels exactly, and therefore
-\begin{align}
- \|A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
- &\le\|V_s^\nu-V_s^\eta\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
-       +|\tau_s^\nu-\tau_s^\eta|\notag\\
- &\le2(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
- \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-two-background-separation}
-\end{align}
-This is the place where retaining the common lower-order jet removes every
-interior contribution from the difference of the backgrounds.
-
-The proxy lower bound is \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-lower-bound}.
-For the actual quotient, the bounded logarithmic gradient of \(p_1\) gives
-\(F_y(z)\ge e^{-L|z|}\), uniformly in \(y\).  Jensen's inequality then yields
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-quotient-positive-lower-bound}
- q_s^\lambda(y)
- \ge\int e^{-L|x|/s}\lambda(\dd x)
- \ge e^{-L\EE_\lambda|X|/s}\longrightarrow1
-\end{equation}
-uniformly in \(y\).  Thus the actual quotients have a common positive lower
-bound.  Their exact split is
-\(q_s^\lambda=A_s^\lambda+\epsilon_sB_r^\lambda+R_s^\lambda\),
-and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-remainder-smallness} supplies the required
-\(L^1\) and \(L^\infty\) smallness.  Finally,
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-entropy-finite} verifies the finite
-positive entropy hypothesis.  All hypotheses of the two-background KL
-perturbation lemma are now proved.  Its conclusion gives
-\[
- D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
- =\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)
- +\frac{s^{-2r}}2\int(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta)^2
-       \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}+o(s^{-2r}).
-\]
-By \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-leading-mode},
-\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the quadratic integral is
-\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition}.  Formula
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-energy} is a relative \(\Phi\)-entropy and
-is therefore nonnegative; the equivalence
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-criterion} follows immediately.
-
-The raw-tail split, its normalization, and the finite-moment dominated
-convergence are exactly the steps that survive from the covariance proof.
-The new step is the two-background expansion above: it retains the common
-lower-order jet inside both positive tail proxies and replaces the
-unavailable one-sided \(\Phi\)-energy of a signed tail difference by a
-relative \(\Phi\)-energy.  When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is
-centred, this energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\),
-which differs from the energy in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by \(o(s^{-4})\), as shown
- in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
+When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is centred, the identified
+energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), which differs
+from the energy in Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by
+\(o(s^{-4})\), as shown in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
 \end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
+bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

-where \(\varepsilon_r\) is bounded on \([0,1]\) and tends to zero at
-zero.  For the uniform part one may use the bounded order-\((r+1)\)
-derivative quotient, giving the stronger \(O(|z|^{r+1})\) bound.  For the
-\(L^1\) part, multiplication by \(p_1(y)\) reduces the integral remainder
-to translates of \(D^rp_1\), exactly as in
-\eqref{eq:stable-local-taylor-modulus}.
-
-Set
+Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} to
+\(p=p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\), whose admissibility is verified in
+Proposition~\ref{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}.  Its measure
+\(\Omega_p\), translate quotient \(F_y^p\), modes \(B_{p,j}^\lambda\),
+proxies \(A_{p,s}^\lambda\), proxy densities \(k_{p,r,s}^\lambda\), and
+quadratic form \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) are, respectively,
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), \(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), \(B_j^\lambda\),
+\(A_s^\lambda\), \(k_{r,s}^\lambda\), and
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}\).  Since both proxies have mass one,
 \[
- q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+ D_{\rm KL}(k_{r,s}^\nu\|k_{r,s}^\eta)
+ =\int A_s^\eta
+   \Phi\!\left(\frac{A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta}{A_s^\eta}\right)
+   \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d},
 \]
-Splitting the integral at \(|x|=s\), retaining the raw exterior translate,
-and using the moment identities gives the exact decomposition
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-exact-quotient-split}
- q_s^\lambda=A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}B_r^\lambda+R_s^\lambda.
-\end{equation}
-Here \(R_s^\lambda\) is the interior Taylor remainder through order \(r\)
-minus the exterior Taylor modes of orders \(1,\ldots,r\).  Equations
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} and
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} imply
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-remainder-smallness}
- \|R_s^\lambda\|_\infty+
- \|R_s^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
-\end{equation}
-Indeed, after multiplication by \(s^r\), the interior term is dominated by
-\(C|x|^r\) and converges pointwise to zero, while for \(j\le r\),
-\[
- s^{-j}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^j\lambda(\dd x)
- \le s^{-r}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x)=o(s^{-r}).
-\]
-The same last estimate gives
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-mass-smallness}
- \tau_s^\lambda=o(s^{-r}).
-\end{equation}
+which identifies \(\mathcal E_{r,s}\).  The abstract theorem now gives
+positivity, finiteness, \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition}, and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-criterion}.  Isotropy gives the
+orthogonal invariance of the quadratic form.  The abstract hypotheses use
+only the displayed order-\(r\) moment, proving the final sentence.
 
-Translation preserves mass, so
-\[
- V_s^\lambda\ge0,\qquad
- \int V_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=\tau_s^\lambda.
-\]
-Also \(\int B_j^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0\), by integration of the
-derivatives in \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-moment-modes}.  Therefore
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-normalization}
- \int A_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=1.
-\end{equation}
-Moreover,
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-lower-bound}
- \inf_yA_s^\lambda(y)
- \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-\tau_s^\lambda\longrightarrow1,
-\end{equation}
-because \(V_s^\lambda\ge0\),
-\(\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty=O(s^{-1})\) (with value zero when \(r=1\)), and
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mass-smallness} holds.  This proves positivity,
-including at \(r=1\), and gives a common lower bound such as \(1/2\).
-
-We next prove proxy-entropy finiteness without appealing to the covariance
-case.  The two-sided stable-density bound in
-Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package} and
-\(1+|w+z|\le(1+|w|)(1+|z|)\) give
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-stable-translate-entropy}
- D_{\rm KL}\!\left(p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)\,\middle\|\,p_1\right)
- \le C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|z|).
-\end{equation}
-If \(\tau_s^\lambda>0\), write \(V_s^\lambda=\tau_s^\lambda Q_s^\lambda\),
-where \(Q_s^\lambda\) is the quotient, relative to \(p_1\), of the
-normalized exterior translate mixture.  Convexity of relative entropy and
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-stable-translate-entropy} imply
-\begin{align}
- \int Q_s^\lambda\log Q_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
- &\le\frac1{\tau_s^\lambda}\int_{|x|>s}
- \left\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|x|/s)\right\}
- \lambda(\dd x)\notag\\
- &<\infty,
- \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}
-\end{align}
-since \(\log(1+|x|/s)\le |x|/s\) and the assumed \(r\)-th moment, with
-\(r\ge1\), supplies a finite first moment.  For \(0\le\tau\le1\),
-\(\Phi(\tau q)\le\tau q\log(1+q)\); hence
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}, together with the bound
-of the negative part of \(q\log q\), proves
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-potential-entropy-finite}
- \int\Phi(V_s^\lambda)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}<\infty.
-\end{equation}
-The conclusion is immediate when \(\tau_s^\lambda=0\).
-
-For large \(s\), \(|C_{r-1,s}-\tau_s^\lambda|\le1/2\), so
-\(A_s^\lambda\le3/2+V_s^\lambda\).  The elementary bound
-\[
- (u+v)\log^+(u+v)\le C\{1+v+\Phi(v)\},
- \qquad 0\le u\le3/2,\quad v\ge0,
-\]
-and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-potential-entropy-finite} show that
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-entropy-finite}
- \int A_s^\lambda\log^+A_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}<\infty.
-\end{equation}
-Finally \(A_s^\eta\ge1/2\).  The positive part of
-\(A_s^\nu\log(A_s^\nu/A_s^\eta)\) is bounded by
-\(A_s^\nu\log^+(2A_s^\nu)\), while its negative part is bounded in absolute
-integral by \(e^{-1}\int A_s^\eta\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=e^{-1}\).
-Thus \(\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)<\infty\), as asserted.
-
-It remains to verify, rather than assume, the hypotheses of the abstract
-two-background KL perturbation lemma.  Put
-\(\epsilon_s=s^{-r}\), take
-\[
- (A_{1,s},A_{2,s})=(A_s^\nu,A_s^\eta),\qquad
- (B_{1,s},B_{2,s})=(B_r^\nu,B_r^\eta),
- \qquad (R_{1,s},R_{2,s})=(R_s^\nu,R_s^\eta).
-\]
-The modes \(B_r^\lambda\) are bounded by
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds}, and their integrals vanish.  The first
-requested background estimate follows directly from the common jet and the
-exact tail normalization:
-\begin{align}
- \|A_s^\lambda-1\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
- &\le\|C_{r-1,s}\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
-      +\|V_s^\lambda-\tau_s^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\notag\\
- &\le \sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}\|B_j^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
-      +2\tau_s^\lambda=o(1).
- \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-background-to-one}
-\end{align}
-For \(r=1\), the sum is empty and the same proof applies.  For the second
-background estimate, the common jet cancels exactly, and therefore
-\begin{align}
- \|A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
- &\le\|V_s^\nu-V_s^\eta\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
-       +|\tau_s^\nu-\tau_s^\eta|\notag\\
- &\le2(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
- \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-two-background-separation}
-\end{align}
-This is the place where retaining the common lower-order jet removes every
-interior contribution from the difference of the backgrounds.
-
-The proxy lower bound is \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-lower-bound}.
-For the actual quotient, the bounded logarithmic gradient of \(p_1\) gives
-\(F_y(z)\ge e^{-L|z|}\), uniformly in \(y\).  Jensen's inequality then yields
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-quotient-positive-lower-bound}
- q_s^\lambda(y)
- \ge\int e^{-L|x|/s}\lambda(\dd x)
- \ge e^{-L\EE_\lambda|X|/s}\longrightarrow1
-\end{equation}
-uniformly in \(y\).  Thus the actual quotients have a common positive lower
-bound.  Their exact split is
-\(q_s^\lambda=A_s^\lambda+\epsilon_sB_r^\lambda+R_s^\lambda\),
-and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-remainder-smallness} supplies the required
-\(L^1\) and \(L^\infty\) smallness.  Finally,
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-entropy-finite} verifies the finite
-positive entropy hypothesis.  All hypotheses of the two-background KL
-perturbation lemma are now proved.  Its conclusion gives
-\[
- D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
- =\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)
- +\frac{s^{-2r}}2\int(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta)^2
-       \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}+o(s^{-2r}).
-\]
-By \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-leading-mode},
-\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the quadratic integral is
-\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition}.  Formula
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-energy} is a relative \(\Phi\)-entropy and
-is therefore nonnegative; the equivalence
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-criterion} follows immediately.
-
-The raw-tail split, its normalization, and the finite-moment dominated
-convergence are exactly the steps that survive from the covariance proof.
-The new step is the two-background expansion above: it retains the common
-lower-order jet inside both positive tail proxies and replaces the
-unavailable one-sided \(\Phi\)-energy of a signed tail difference by a
-relative \(\Phi\)-energy.  When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is
-centred, this energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\),
-which differs from the energy in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by \(o(s^{-4})\), as shown
- in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
+When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is centred, the identified
+energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), which differs
+from the energy in Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by
+\(o(s^{-4})\), as shown in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
 \end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
+\item invertible affine images;
+\item finite tensor products, allowing different block dimensions; and
+\item finite positive mixtures of admissible densities on the same space.
+\end{enumerate}
+The criterion of Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel}
+therefore applies to every kernel obtained by finitely combining these
+operations.  Its base members include, at every order, each isotropic
+strictly \(\alpha\)-stable density, \(0<\alpha<2\), the Poisson kernel in
+every dimension, and every multivariate Student kernel
 \[

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
+bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

- \int A_s^\lambda\log^+A_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}<\infty.
-\end{equation}
-Finally \(A_s^\eta\ge1/2\).  The positive part of
-\(A_s^\nu\log(A_s^\nu/A_s^\eta)\) is bounded by
-\(A_s^\nu\log^+(2A_s^\nu)\), while its negative part is bounded in absolute
-integral by \(e^{-1}\int A_s^\eta\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=e^{-1}\).
-Thus \(\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)<\infty\), as asserted.
-
-It remains to verify, rather than assume, the hypotheses of the abstract
-two-background KL perturbation lemma.  Put
-\(\epsilon_s=s^{-r}\), take
-\[
- (A_{1,s},A_{2,s})=(A_s^\nu,A_s^\eta),\qquad
- (B_{1,s},B_{2,s})=(B_r^\nu,B_r^\eta),
- \qquad (R_{1,s},R_{2,s})=(R_s^\nu,R_s^\eta).
-\]
-The modes \(B_r^\lambda\) are bounded by
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds}, and their integrals vanish.  The first
-requested background estimate follows directly from the common jet and the
-exact tail normalization:
-\begin{align}
- \|A_s^\lambda-1\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
- &\le\|C_{r-1,s}\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
-      +\|V_s^\lambda-\tau_s^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\notag\\
- &\le \sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}\|B_j^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
-      +2\tau_s^\lambda=o(1).
- \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-background-to-one}
-\end{align}
-For \(r=1\), the sum is empty and the same proof applies.  For the second
-background estimate, the common jet cancels exactly, and therefore
-\begin{align}
- \|A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
- &\le\|V_s^\nu-V_s^\eta\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
-       +|\tau_s^\nu-\tau_s^\eta|\notag\\
- &\le2(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
- \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-two-background-separation}
-\end{align}
-This is the place where retaining the common lower-order jet removes every
-interior contribution from the difference of the backgrounds.
-
-The proxy lower bound is \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-lower-bound}.
-For the actual quotient, the bounded logarithmic gradient of \(p_1\) gives
-\(F_y(z)\ge e^{-L|z|}\), uniformly in \(y\).  Jensen's inequality then yields
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-quotient-positive-lower-bound}
- q_s^\lambda(y)
- \ge\int e^{-L|x|/s}\lambda(\dd x)
- \ge e^{-L\EE_\lambda|X|/s}\longrightarrow1
-\end{equation}
-uniformly in \(y\).  Thus the actual quotients have a common positive lower
-bound.  Their exact split is
-\(q_s^\lambda=A_s^\lambda+\epsilon_sB_r^\lambda+R_s^\lambda\),
-and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-remainder-smallness} supplies the required
-\(L^1\) and \(L^\infty\) smallness.  Finally,
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-entropy-finite} verifies the finite
-positive entropy hypothesis.  All hypotheses of the two-background KL
-perturbation lemma are now proved.  Its conclusion gives
-\[
- D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
- =\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)
- +\frac{s^{-2r}}2\int(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta)^2
-       \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}+o(s^{-2r}).
-\]
-By \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-leading-mode},
-\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the quadratic integral is
-\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition}.  Formula
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-energy} is a relative \(\Phi\)-entropy and
-is therefore nonnegative; the equivalence
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-criterion} follows immediately.
-
-The raw-tail split, its normalization, and the finite-moment dominated
-convergence are exactly the steps that survive from the covariance proof.
-The new step is the two-background expansion above: it retains the common
-lower-order jet inside both positive tail proxies and replaces the
-unavailable one-sided \(\Phi\)-energy of a signed tail difference by a
-relative \(\Phi\)-energy.  When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is
-centred, this energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\),
-which differs from the energy in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by \(o(s^{-4})\), as shown
- in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
+When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is centred, the identified
+energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), which differs
+from the energy in Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by
+\(o(s^{-4})\), as shown in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
 \end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
+bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

- q_s^\lambda=A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}B_r^\lambda+R_s^\lambda.
-\end{equation}
-Here \(R_s^\lambda\) is the interior Taylor remainder through order \(r\)
-minus the exterior Taylor modes of orders \(1,\ldots,r\).  Equations
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} and
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} imply
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-remainder-smallness}
- \|R_s^\lambda\|_\infty+
- \|R_s^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
-\end{equation}
-Indeed, after multiplication by \(s^r\), the interior term is dominated by
-\(C|x|^r\) and converges pointwise to zero, while for \(j\le r\),
-\[
- s^{-j}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^j\lambda(\dd x)
- \le s^{-r}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x)=o(s^{-r}).
-\]
-The same last estimate gives
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-mass-smallness}
- \tau_s^\lambda=o(s^{-r}).
-\end{equation}
+which identifies \(\mathcal E_{r,s}\).  The abstract theorem now gives
+positivity, finiteness, \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition}, and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-criterion}.  Isotropy gives the
+orthogonal invariance of the quadratic form.  The abstract hypotheses use
+only the displayed order-\(r\) moment, proving the final sentence.
 
-Translation preserves mass, so
-\[
- V_s^\lambda\ge0,\qquad
- \int V_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=\tau_s^\lambda.
-\]
-Also \(\int B_j^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0\), by integration of the
-derivatives in \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-moment-modes}.  Therefore
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-normalization}
- \int A_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=1.
-\end{equation}
-Moreover,
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-lower-bound}
- \inf_yA_s^\lambda(y)
- \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-\tau_s^\lambda\longrightarrow1,
-\end{equation}
-because \(V_s^\lambda\ge0\),
-\(\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty=O(s^{-1})\) (with value zero when \(r=1\)), and
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mass-smallness} holds.  This proves positivity,
-including at \(r=1\), and gives a common lower bound such as \(1/2\).
-
-We next prove proxy-entropy finiteness without appealing to the covariance
-case.  The two-sided stable-density bound in
-Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package} and
-\(1+|w+z|\le(1+|w|)(1+|z|)\) give
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-stable-translate-entropy}
- D_{\rm KL}\!\left(p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)\,\middle\|\,p_1\right)
- \le C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|z|).
-\end{equation}
-If \(\tau_s^\lambda>0\), write \(V_s^\lambda=\tau_s^\lambda Q_s^\lambda\),
-where \(Q_s^\lambda\) is the quotient, relative to \(p_1\), of the
-normalized exterior translate mixture.  Convexity of relative entropy and
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-stable-translate-entropy} imply
-\begin{align}
- \int Q_s^\lambda\log Q_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
- &\le\frac1{\tau_s^\lambda}\int_{|x|>s}
- \left\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|x|/s)\right\}
- \lambda(\dd x)\notag\\
- &<\infty,
- \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}
-\end{align}
-since \(\log(1+|x|/s)\le |x|/s\) and the assumed \(r\)-th moment, with
-\(r\ge1\), supplies a finite first moment.  For \(0\le\tau\le1\),
-\(\Phi(\tau q)\le\tau q\log(1+q)\); hence
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}, together with the bound
-of the negative part of \(q\log q\), proves
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-potential-entropy-finite}
- \int\Phi(V_s^\lambda)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}<\infty.
-\end{equation}
-The conclusion is immediate when \(\tau_s^\lambda=0\).
-
-For large \(s\), \(|C_{r-1,s}-\tau_s^\lambda|\le1/2\), so
-\(A_s^\lambda\le3/2+V_s^\lambda\).  The elementary bound
-\[
- (u+v)\log^+(u+v)\le C\{1+v+\Phi(v)\},
- \qquad 0\le u\le3/2,\quad v\ge0,
-\]
-and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-potential-entropy-finite} show that
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-entropy-finite}
- \int A_s^\lambda\log^+A_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}<\infty.
-\end{equation}
-Finally \(A_s^\eta\ge1/2\).  The positive part of
-\(A_s^\nu\log(A_s^\nu/A_s^\eta)\) is bounded by
-\(A_s^\nu\log^+(2A_s^\nu)\), while its negative part is bounded in absolute
-integral by \(e^{-1}\int A_s^\eta\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=e^{-1}\).
-Thus \(\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)<\infty\), as asserted.
-
-It remains to verify, rather than assume, the hypotheses of the abstract
-two-background KL perturbation lemma.  Put
-\(\epsilon_s=s^{-r}\), take
-\[
- (A_{1,s},A_{2,s})=(A_s^\nu,A_s^\eta),\qquad
- (B_{1,s},B_{2,s})=(B_r^\nu,B_r^\eta),
- \qquad (R_{1,s},R_{2,s})=(R_s^\nu,R_s^\eta).
-\]
-The modes \(B_r^\lambda\) are bounded by
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds}, and their integrals vanish.  The first
-requested background estimate follows directly from the common jet and the
-exact tail normalization:
-\begin{align}
- \|A_s^\lambda-1\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
- &\le\|C_{r-1,s}\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
-      +\|V_s^\lambda-\tau_s^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\notag\\
- &\le \sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}\|B_j^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
-      +2\tau_s^\lambda=o(1).
- \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-background-to-one}
-\end{align}
-For \(r=1\), the sum is empty and the same proof applies.  For the second
-background estimate, the common jet cancels exactly, and therefore
-\begin{align}
- \|A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
- &\le\|V_s^\nu-V_s^\eta\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
-       +|\tau_s^\nu-\tau_s^\eta|\notag\\
- &\le2(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
- \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-two-background-separation}
-\end{align}
-This is the place where retaining the common lower-order jet removes every
-interior contribution from the difference of the backgrounds.
-
-The proxy lower bound is \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-lower-bound}.
-For the actual quotient, the bounded logarithmic gradient of \(p_1\) gives
-\(F_y(z)\ge e^{-L|z|}\), uniformly in \(y\).  Jensen's inequality then yields
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-quotient-positive-lower-bound}
- q_s^\lambda(y)
- \ge\int e^{-L|x|/s}\lambda(\dd x)
- \ge e^{-L\EE_\lambda|X|/s}\longrightarrow1
-\end{equation}
-uniformly in \(y\).  Thus the actual quotients have a common positive lower
-bound.  Their exact split is
-\(q_s^\lambda=A_s^\lambda+\epsilon_sB_r^\lambda+R_s^\lambda\),
-and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-remainder-smallness} supplies the required
-\(L^1\) and \(L^\infty\) smallness.  Finally,
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-entropy-finite} verifies the finite
-positive entropy hypothesis.  All hypotheses of the two-background KL
-perturbation lemma are now proved.  Its conclusion gives
-\[
- D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
- =\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)
- +\frac{s^{-2r}}2\int(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta)^2
-       \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}+o(s^{-2r}).
-\]
-By \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-leading-mode},
-\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the quadratic integral is
-\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition}.  Formula
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-energy} is a relative \(\Phi\)-entropy and
-is therefore nonnegative; the equivalence
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-criterion} follows immediately.
-
-The raw-tail split, its normalization, and the finite-moment dominated
-convergence are exactly the steps that survive from the covariance proof.
-The new step is the two-background expansion above: it retains the common
-lower-order jet inside both positive tail proxies and replaces the
-unavailable one-sided \(\Phi\)-energy of a signed tail difference by a
-relative \(\Phi\)-energy.  When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is
-centred, this energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\),
-which differs from the energy in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by \(o(s^{-4})\), as shown
- in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
+When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is centred, the identified
+energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), which differs
+from the energy in Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by
+\(o(s^{-4})\), as shown in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
 \end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Bounded score implies finite translate entropy]

+\begin{proof}

+calculus bounds the absolute value of the logarithm by \(L|z|\); integration
+and nonnegativity of relative entropy give
+\eqref{eq:bounded-score-translate-entropy}.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
+bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

-first-unmatched-moment theorem recalled above uses a different weighted
-Hermite mechanism; it is not presented as a member of the positive
-tail-proxy theorem.
+This stable statement is the exact specialization of the numbered abstract
+kernel Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel}.  That theorem
+gives a sufficient kernel criterion: bounded normalized derivatives through
+order \(r\) and quotient-uniform continuity at the top order.  Its bounded
+score already implies finite translate entropy with linear growth, so no
+separate entropy hypothesis is imposed.  Proposition
+\ref{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples} verifies stable, Poisson, and
+multivariate Student kernels and proves closure under invertible affine
+images, finite products, and finite positive mixtures.  No tail asymptotic or
+regular variation enters the abstract proof.  Proposition
+\ref{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary} locates Gaussian
+smoothing in a different proxy geometry: this theorem is the
+bounded-score/additive branch, whereas the Gaussian requires an
+unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score Hermite branch.  The
+Gaussian result recalled above is therefore not claimed as coverage by the
+positive tail-proxy theorem.

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
+\item invertible affine images;
+\item finite tensor products, allowing different block dimensions; and
+\item finite positive mixtures of admissible densities on the same space.
+\end{enumerate}

+therefore applies to every kernel obtained by finitely combining these

+strictly \(\alpha\)-stable density, \(0<\alpha<2\), the Poisson kernel in
+every dimension, and every multivariate Student kernel
 \[

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the

+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.

-Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by \(o(s^{-4})\), as shown
- in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
+When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is centred, the identified
+energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), which differs
+from the energy in Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by
+\(o(s^{-4})\), as shown in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
 \end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Zero mass of integrable density derivatives]
+If \(p\in C^r(\RR^d)\) and \(\partial^\gamma p\in L^1\) for
+\(|\gamma|\le r\), then
+\[
+ \int_{\RR^d}\partial^\gamma p(y)\dd y=0,
+ \qquad 1\le|\gamma|\le r.
+\]
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Choose \(j\) with \(\gamma_j>0\), put
+\(f=\partial^{\gamma-e_j}p\in W^{1,1}\), and test
+\(\partial_jf\) against cutoffs \(\chi_R\to1\) with
+\(\|\nabla\chi_R\|_\infty=O(R^{-1})\).  Then
+\(\int\chi_R\partial_jf=-\int f\partial_j\chi_R\to0\), while dominated
+convergence sends the left side to \(\int\partial_jf\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Bounded score implies finite translate entropy]
+\label{lem:bounded-score-translate-entropy}
+If \(p>0\), \(p\in C^1(\RR^d)\), and
+\(\|\nabla\log p\|_\infty\le L\), then, for every \(z\in\RR^d\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:bounded-score-translate-entropy}
+ 0\le D_{\rm KL}\bigl(p(\mathord\cdot-z)\|p\bigr)\le L|z|.

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
+bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
+\item invertible affine images;
+\item finite tensor products, allowing different block dimensions; and
+\item finite positive mixtures of admissible densities on the same space.

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus

+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.

-unavailable one-sided \(\Phi\)-energy of a signed tail difference by a
-relative \(\Phi\)-energy.  When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is
-centred, this energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\),
-which differs from the energy in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by \(o(s^{-4})\), as shown
- in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
+When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is centred, the identified
+energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), which differs
+from the energy in Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by
+\(o(s^{-4})\), as shown in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
 \end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
+bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

- \le s^{-r}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x)=o(s^{-r}).
-\]
-The same last estimate gives
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-mass-smallness}
- \tau_s^\lambda=o(s^{-r}).
-\end{equation}
+which identifies \(\mathcal E_{r,s}\).  The abstract theorem now gives
+positivity, finiteness, \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition}, and
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-criterion}.  Isotropy gives the
+orthogonal invariance of the quadratic form.  The abstract hypotheses use
+only the displayed order-\(r\) moment, proving the final sentence.
 
-Translation preserves mass, so
-\[
- V_s^\lambda\ge0,\qquad
- \int V_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=\tau_s^\lambda.
-\]
-Also \(\int B_j^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0\), by integration of the
-derivatives in \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-moment-modes}.  Therefore
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-normalization}
- \int A_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=1.
-\end{equation}
-Moreover,
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-lower-bound}
- \inf_yA_s^\lambda(y)
- \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-\tau_s^\lambda\longrightarrow1,
-\end{equation}
-because \(V_s^\lambda\ge0\),
-\(\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty=O(s^{-1})\) (with value zero when \(r=1\)), and
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mass-smallness} holds.  This proves positivity,
-including at \(r=1\), and gives a common lower bound such as \(1/2\).
-
-We next prove proxy-entropy finiteness without appealing to the covariance
-case.  The two-sided stable-density bound in
-Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package} and
-\(1+|w+z|\le(1+|w|)(1+|z|)\) give
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-stable-translate-entropy}
- D_{\rm KL}\!\left(p_1(\mathord\cdot-z)\,\middle\|\,p_1\right)
- \le C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|z|).
-\end{equation}
-If \(\tau_s^\lambda>0\), write \(V_s^\lambda=\tau_s^\lambda Q_s^\lambda\),
-where \(Q_s^\lambda\) is the quotient, relative to \(p_1\), of the
-normalized exterior translate mixture.  Convexity of relative entropy and
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-stable-translate-entropy} imply
-\begin{align}
- \int Q_s^\lambda\log Q_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
- &\le\frac1{\tau_s^\lambda}\int_{|x|>s}
- \left\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|x|/s)\right\}
- \lambda(\dd x)\notag\\
- &<\infty,
- \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}
-\end{align}
-since \(\log(1+|x|/s)\le |x|/s\) and the assumed \(r\)-th moment, with
-\(r\ge1\), supplies a finite first moment.  For \(0\le\tau\le1\),
-\(\Phi(\tau q)\le\tau q\log(1+q)\); hence
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}, together with the bound
-of the negative part of \(q\log q\), proves
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-potential-entropy-finite}
- \int\Phi(V_s^\lambda)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}<\infty.
-\end{equation}
-The conclusion is immediate when \(\tau_s^\lambda=0\).
-
-For large \(s\), \(|C_{r-1,s}-\tau_s^\lambda|\le1/2\), so
-\(A_s^\lambda\le3/2+V_s^\lambda\).  The elementary bound
-\[
- (u+v)\log^+(u+v)\le C\{1+v+\Phi(v)\},
- \qquad 0\le u\le3/2,\quad v\ge0,
-\]
-and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-potential-entropy-finite} show that
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-entropy-finite}
- \int A_s^\lambda\log^+A_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}<\infty.
-\end{equation}
-Finally \(A_s^\eta\ge1/2\).  The positive part of
-\(A_s^\nu\log(A_s^\nu/A_s^\eta)\) is bounded by
-\(A_s^\nu\log^+(2A_s^\nu)\), while its negative part is bounded in absolute
-integral by \(e^{-1}\int A_s^\eta\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=e^{-1}\).
-Thus \(\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)<\infty\), as asserted.
-
-It remains to verify, rather than assume, the hypotheses of the abstract
-two-background KL perturbation lemma.  Put
-\(\epsilon_s=s^{-r}\), take
-\[
- (A_{1,s},A_{2,s})=(A_s^\nu,A_s^\eta),\qquad
- (B_{1,s},B_{2,s})=(B_r^\nu,B_r^\eta),
- \qquad (R_{1,s},R_{2,s})=(R_s^\nu,R_s^\eta).
-\]
-The modes \(B_r^\lambda\) are bounded by
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds}, and their integrals vanish.  The first
-requested background estimate follows directly from the common jet and the
-exact tail normalization:
-\begin{align}
- \|A_s^\lambda-1\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
- &\le\|C_{r-1,s}\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
-      +\|V_s^\lambda-\tau_s^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\notag\\
- &\le \sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}\|B_j^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
-      +2\tau_s^\lambda=o(1).
- \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-background-to-one}
-\end{align}
-For \(r=1\), the sum is empty and the same proof applies.  For the second
-background estimate, the common jet cancels exactly, and therefore
-\begin{align}
- \|A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
- &\le\|V_s^\nu-V_s^\eta\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
-       +|\tau_s^\nu-\tau_s^\eta|\notag\\
- &\le2(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
- \label{eq:arbitrary-tail-two-background-separation}
-\end{align}
-This is the place where retaining the common lower-order jet removes every
-interior contribution from the difference of the backgrounds.
-
-The proxy lower bound is \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-lower-bound}.
-For the actual quotient, the bounded logarithmic gradient of \(p_1\) gives
-\(F_y(z)\ge e^{-L|z|}\), uniformly in \(y\).  Jensen's inequality then yields
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:arbitrary-tail-quotient-positive-lower-bound}
- q_s^\lambda(y)
- \ge\int e^{-L|x|/s}\lambda(\dd x)
- \ge e^{-L\EE_\lambda|X|/s}\longrightarrow1
-\end{equation}
-uniformly in \(y\).  Thus the actual quotients have a common positive lower
-bound.  Their exact split is
-\(q_s^\lambda=A_s^\lambda+\epsilon_sB_r^\lambda+R_s^\lambda\),
-and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-remainder-smallness} supplies the required
-\(L^1\) and \(L^\infty\) smallness.  Finally,
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-positive-entropy-finite} verifies the finite
-positive entropy hypothesis.  All hypotheses of the two-background KL
-perturbation lemma are now proved.  Its conclusion gives
-\[
- D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
- =\mathcal E_{r,s}(\nu,\eta)
- +\frac{s^{-2r}}2\int(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta)^2
-       \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}+o(s^{-2r}).
-\]
-By \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-leading-mode},
-\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the quadratic integral is
-\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-decomposition}.  Formula
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-energy} is a relative \(\Phi\)-entropy and
-is therefore nonnegative; the equivalence
-\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-defect-criterion} follows immediately.
-
-The raw-tail split, its normalization, and the finite-moment dominated
-convergence are exactly the steps that survive from the covariance proof.
-The new step is the two-background expansion above: it retains the common
-lower-order jet inside both positive tail proxies and replaces the
-unavailable one-sided \(\Phi\)-energy of a signed tail difference by a
-relative \(\Phi\)-energy.  When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is
-centred, this energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\),
-which differs from the energy in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by \(o(s^{-4})\), as shown
- in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
+When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is centred, the identified
+energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), which differs
+from the energy in Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by
+\(o(s^{-4})\), as shown in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
 \end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Zero mass of integrable density derivatives]
+If \(p\in C^r(\RR^d)\) and \(\partial^\gamma p\in L^1\) for
+\(|\gamma|\le r\), then
+\[
+ \int_{\RR^d}\partial^\gamma p(y)\dd y=0,
+ \qquad 1\le|\gamma|\le r.
+\]
+\end{unnumberedlemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Choose \(j\) with \(\gamma_j>0\), put
+\(f=\partial^{\gamma-e_j}p\in W^{1,1}\), and test
+\(\partial_jf\) against cutoffs \(\chi_R\to1\) with
+\(\|\nabla\chi_R\|_\infty=O(R^{-1})\).  Then
+\(\int\chi_R\partial_jf=-\int f\partial_j\chi_R\to0\), while dominated
+convergence sends the left side to \(\int\partial_jf\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Bounded-score translate entropy]
+If \(p>0\), \(p\in C^1(\RR^d)\), and
+\(\|\nabla\log p\|_\infty\le L\), then, for every \(z\in\RR^d\),
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:bounded-score-translate-entropy}
+ 0\le D_{\rm KL}\bigl(p(\mathord\cdot-z)\|p\bigr)\le L|z|.
+\end{equation}
+\end{unnumberedlemma}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
+bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
+\item invertible affine images;
+\item finite tensor products, allowing different block dimensions; and
+\item finite positive mixtures of admissible densities on the same space.

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the

+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.

-Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by \(o(s^{-4})\), as shown
- in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
+When \(r=2\), \(\eta=\delta_0\), and \(\nu\) is centred, the identified
+energy is \(\int\Phi(V_s^\nu-\tau_s^\nu)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), which differs
+from the energy in Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} by
+\(o(s^{-4})\), as shown in \eqref{eq:stable-remove-mass}.
 \end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
+bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}

+\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
+\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
+For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
+\item invertible affine images;
+\item finite tensor products, allowing different block dimensions; and
+\item finite positive mixtures of admissible densities on the same space.
+\end{enumerate}

+therefore applies to every kernel obtained by finitely combining these

+every dimension, and every multivariate Student kernel

+\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
+\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
+The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
+strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
+prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
+bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
+belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
+branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
+boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
+\end{proposition}
